answer: Enrolment binds an identity to a room. The client plays a chirp, records the decay; the verifier deconvolves it out, leaving reflections and a reverberant tail. A vaulted hallway harbors brighter flutter than carpeted rooms, and the curve holds. Curves within three percent fold two wallets into one vote. A farm can forge one curve, but a re-probe at payout matches the tail to the live noise floor. A thousand genuine rooms cost a thousand leases, near $300,000 yearly. A superintendent knows his stairwell by its echo; sparrows sound alike on every balcony, yet balconies answer differently.
